notes.title: Keyboard support now live, and thank you play testers!
notes.notes: [p]Good morning! Last week I announced the release of the playtest and the response has honestly blown me away. Currently, [b]593 [/b]of you have access, and [b]157[/b] of you have played it! I was expecting maybe a dozen or so people to be interested in my little game, so those numbers are honestly fantastic.[/p][p][/p][p]I've also had lots of lovely people join my Discord ([url="https://discord.gg/j3TdUAUuHr"]https://discord.gg/j3TdUAUuHr[/url]) who have left some fantastic feedback and extremely useful bug reports. Thank you to every single one of you who has joined so far.[/p][p][/p][p]However, I've learnt a harsh lesson, as the biggest piece of feedback was the disappointment in the lack of keyboard support. I stubbornly thought that just because I think it plays much better with a controller, that others shouldn't be able to play with anything else. Looking back, this just reduces the games audience unnecessarily, so this week I have properly implemented keyboard support. While I still recommend playing with controller, I am pleasantly surprised how decent it feels to play on keyboard too.[/p][p][/p][p]If you were interested in playing but didn't have a controller, I hope now I can tempt you back to give it a go![/p][p][/p][p]Thanks all, see you next time.[/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44732917/631b071324cc0ef235d5d1cf963e9b937bf70624.png"][/img][/p]

notes.title: Playtest now live!
notes.notes: [p]Hello community![/p][p][/p][p]It's with massive excitement that I can finally announce that the first playable version of Vitrified is now live! It has been years of work to get to this point, and the thought of real people finally playing my game is truly awesome. If you want to play yourself, simply request to join using the invite on the store page. The only thing to mention is that it is controller only, but you can play on Windows, Mac or Linux (Steam Deck!).[/p][p][/p][p]Some close friends have already played and I've done an awful lot of testing, so hopefully the game has less bugs than you might expect from a playtest build. However, if you do find a bug, I would massively appreciate if you told me about it on the games [b]Discord:[/b] [url="https://discord.gg/j3TdUAUuHr"]https://discord.gg/j3TdUAUuHr[/url][/p][p][/p][p]As well as bugs, I'd love to hear anything and everything you have to say about the game on the Discord, good or bad! I value every piece of feedback, and want to make the best game I possibly can, so all feedback plays a massive part in the future of Vitrified. I'll also be posting more regular development updates there.[/p][p][/p][p]In terms of actual game, a massive amount of content has been made to get it into a state where you the player get a worthwhile experience from the playtest. I have added two new enemies - wolves and giant spiders, added a whole new area with an NPC who gives you a quest, vastly expanded the underground tunnels, and added a host of secret areas. So far, the average play time has been about an hour to do the one quest, which I'm honestly really proud of, and I really hope you will enjoy your time in the world of Vitrified too.[/p][p][/p][p]So what's next? Well with this playtest I am hoping to chisel the starting area and core mechanics into a state that provides players with a fun and memorable experience, which I will then release as the demo. From there, I will start expanding the world and game content towards the full game. Plans for the rest of The Wasteland and the story behind the player and ALANs journey has been in development for a long time, and I am so excited to finally set my sights on the full game. Right now, I am really hoping that I can get to that point by the end of 2026.[/p][p][/p][p]Thank you for following along with the journey of Vitrified. Your interest in my game honestly means the world to me. See you soon, and please enjoy the playtest![/p][p][/p][p][img src="{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/44732917/86aea829088101ac34399df75543c7a42cf6f84a.jpg"][/img][/p][p][/p]

notes.title: New name, new art and a demo approaches
notes.notes:
Hello community! It's been a busy but productive few months, and we have lot's to discuss!

First, you may be wondering, what on earth is 'Vitrified' and why am I seeing community updates for it? Well, that's because 'Father of AI' has had a name change, but I promise it is still the same game, with the same setting, same story, and same mechanics. 'Vitrified' is just a better fit, is less clunky, and in my opinion, sounds cooler. If you know what vitrification means, and more importantly, what causes it, that may give a clue to a key part of the story ;)

Along with a new name, you may notice the snazzy new key art, which depicts the player and ALAN facing down one of the mighty giant sand worms, which have become the poster child of the game. With that brings a host of comparisons to Dune, which I welcome and have enjoyed! The world of Dune is one of my biggest inspirations after all.

Now, progress. I had a couple of less productive months at the end of 2024, but 2025 has been full steam ahead. At the last post, no areas in the game could be called complete. Now, we have two major areas that are finished and another that is close. Along with a host of ALAN teamwork mechanics, new mutant enemies and proper survival mechanics, 'worm fields' have been invented. Finally there is a way to interact with the worms, and I'm very proud of how fun they are to navigate. I won't spoil the mechanics involved, [i]just watch your step.[/i]

So lots of progress has been made, and the game has a new identity. What next? One word - demo. The very thought of finally releasing something playable both excites and frightens me, but I can assure you it is not too far away. My goal of releasing a demo for the June Next Fest is now looking slightly less likely, but a summer release date feels very much on the cards.

Thank you for sticking with me and following the progress of my weird little game. I appreciate you more than you know. Until next time.

notes.title: Sand worms, survival and Next Fest
notes.notes:
Hello community! I'm very excited to share that much progress has been made in the past few months.

First off, I've conducted a fairly major re-design of the game as a whole. Previously, the plan was for it to be a purely linear adventure, but now it is an open-world survival adventure. The story and core mechanics remain largely the same, but I realised focusing on exploration and survival makes a lot more sense for the game I am trying to make. Plus, the post-apocalyptic wasteland is naturally very conducive to the new survival elements! The story will reveal itself slowly as you explore the world and get closer to escaping the wasteland.

Because of this re-design, I've had to re make a fair amount of content, but it's already feeling better and more interesting than ever! One bit of content I'm proud of is the opening scene of the game, which reveals why you find yourself in the middle of the wasteland, and how you come to meet ALAN, your trusty robot companion.

As well as new content, I'm also very happy with the newly implemented survival mechanics. In particular, the thirst mechanic. It feels tactile and satisfying to finally find a source of water and refill your bottle, and the necessity of finding water forces you to explore more of the world, including the mysterious underground tunnels...

With all of this progress I'm keen to keep up the momentum, so I have set myself the target of getting a demo ready for the Steam Next Fest in June! There is a whole lot to do by then but if I keep this current momentum I am optimistic that it will be ready.

Finally, I'm excited to share a spectacular new enemy made by my brilliant artist Matteo. Thanks for checking in!
